archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A team with the league's best lineup and the margin of a mid-90s-win club that finished 89-73, lost about six games to close-game results, and was swept out of the Wild Card round after scoring one run.

report.headline: Baseball's best offense, a 95-win margin, and one run in October

recap.finish: 89-73, second in the NL Central; lost the NLWC 0-2 to SD
recap.body:
The record says a solid second-place team, 14 games behind Milwaukee's 103 wins. The underlying numbers describe something better. Chicago outscored opponents by 147 runs, the third-best Run Diff / G in baseball at +0.91. It scored the most runs per game in the league with the top team OPS (.767), and it did that in a home park that plays below average for hitters (96). Its fielders saved 72.8 runs, also first. W vs Run Diff puts the shortfall at 5.9 wins, so the margin was that of a roughly 95-win team.

The season came in waves. A 17-9 April gave way to a 13-16 May, the only month before September when the Cubs were outscored (131 allowed to 115 scored). From June through August they went 46-32, and August was the peak: 178 runs in 28 games, more than six a night. The year included both a 10-game winning streak and a 10-game losing streak, which fits the up-and-down shape. September went 11-13, and the scoring fell to 4.5 runs a game. Over the last 10 games the team went 5-5 and scored two runs or fewer four times, which turned out to be a preview.

Pete Crow-Armstrong was the engine. He put up 10.6 WAR, 45 homers, 41 steals, a 157 wRC+ and 21.1 Def Runs, and he ranks first among 182 outfielders on the site. Seiya Suzuki (134 wRC+) and Alex Bregman (128) added another 10.1 WAR between them. The A+ lineup grade reflects that the order was solid deep into the lineup, not just at the top. Defense ran through the whole roster. Dansby Swanson was worth 3.4 WAR with a 93 wRC+ largely on 11.3 Def Runs. The soft spots were at the plate up the middle: Swanson and Nico Hoerner (.316 OBP, 88 wRC+) both hit below average.

The staff is where a 95-win profile became 89 wins. A 4.12 ERA ranked 14th even behind the league's best defense, which says the pitching itself was weaker than that number. The rotation graded C+. All five starters made at least 22 starts, but none ranked higher than 42nd on the starter tab, and their luck ran in both directions. Kevin Gausman's 4.51 ERA sat on a 3.74 FIP, while Shota Imanaga's 3.77 ERA hid a 4.47 FIP. The D+ bullpen leaned on swingmen Aaron Civale and Javier Assad for about 205 innings, both with strikeout rates under 19%. Ryan Zeferjahn walked 13.2% of batters. The best reliever, Ben Brown (1.85 ERA in 68 innings), ended the year on the 60-day injured list. A pen that thin is a plausible reason for the record falling short of the run differential.

The ending was quick. At San Diego the Cubs lost 8-0 and 4-1: one run in two games and a .374 postseason OPS, last among playoff teams. Crow-Armstrong and Bregman went a combined 0-for-16, and Hoerner was the only regular who hit. Matthew Boyd and Gausman were both knocked out before the fifth inning. After a 2025 that produced four playoff wins on almost the same run differential, this year produced none.

highlights.title: Best lineup in baseball
highlights.body: The Cubs led the league in runs per game and OPS while playing in a park that suppresses offense, and the hitters graded A+. Crow-Armstrong's 10.6 WAR season sat on top of a deep group: Suzuki and Bregman were both well above average, and seven regulars posted a wRC+ of 103 or better. Offense ranked fifth in 2025, so this is a step forward, but a season this large from one player is hard to repeat.

highlights.title: Defense kept getting better
highlights.body: Fielding Runs climbed for a fourth straight year, from 41.8 in 2025 to 72.8 and first in the league. The value came from across the field: Crow-Armstrong, Swanson, Suzuki, Happ, Hoerner and Bregman all saved runs. This is a stable, multi-year trait rather than a fluke.

highlights.title: A contender's run differential
highlights.body: At +0.91 runs a game, third in baseball, Chicago played like a club well above its 89 wins. June through August went 46-32, with August's 178 runs the high-water mark. The margin matched 2025's almost exactly, so the underlying quality held steady.

lowlights.title: A thin, middling pitching staff
lowlights.body: ERA ranked 14th even with the league's best defense behind it. The rotation graded C+ with no starter in the top 40 of the starter tab, and the bullpen graded D+. The pen's best arm, Ben Brown, finished on the 60-day injured list. This is the group that keeps the team from matching its offense.

lowlights.title: Losing close games, again
lowlights.body: A W vs Run Diff of -5.9 ranked 26th. It is the fourth straight year below expectation: -7.2, -5.1, -3.7, now -5.9. The stat is mostly luck, but four years in a row alongside a weak bullpen suggests at least part of it is late-inning pitching.

lowlights.title: The bats went quiet late
lowlights.body: September scoring fell to 4.5 runs a game from August's 6.4, and the playoff lineup managed one run and a .374 OPS in two games. Two games is a tiny sample, but the fade began weeks earlier.

arc.note: A 17-9 April, a losing May, a strong June-through-August run peaking in August, then an 11-13 September that carried straight into a two-game Wild Card exit. Along the way the team had both a 10-game winning streak and a 10-game losing streak.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is real and repeatable in two places: an A+ lineup and a defense that has improved four years running. The offense still leans hard on Crow-Armstrong, and expecting another 10.6 WAR is optimistic. Hoerner and Swanson are glove-first bats who leave room for more production at the plate. Pitching is where the work is. The rotation has innings but no front-line starter. Gausman's FIP says he was better than his ERA, while Imanaga's says he was fortunate. The D+ bullpen needs strikeout arms beyond Zeferjahn and Webb, plus Brown back healthy. The 5.9-win gap to the run differential should mostly regress, but four straight years of it argue that fixing the late innings, not waiting on luck, is how this margin turns into the wins it implies.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the playoff read rests on just two games.
